description: The presentation: its theme, slides, and settings. Its `locale` writes the date field and reads its own charts' cells; a theme's charts read theirs as en-US. Where MarkdownPoint can't write dates in the locale, it warns and writes them in en-US. Changing `locale` in MarkdownPoint respells the presentation's chart cells, and an edit of the file alone doesn't. It also says where words break into pieces as they animate, and which forms Chinese, Japanese, and Korean characters take.

markdownpoint.description: The format version, its major and minor in quotes: "1.0". MarkdownPoint 1.x opens any version 1.x file. A newer major needs a newer MarkdownPoint.

id.description: The presentation's id, which the .md file repeats; a copy made outside MarkdownPoint keeps it, and with it its view link, until MarkdownPoint gives the copy one of its own.

save.description: A save stamp: the id of a save. MarkdownPoint writes it while the presentation is shared for editing, to tell this file apart from an older copy with the same content. Other tools keep it as it is.

theme.description: The key of the presentation's theme, the name of its folder in themes. Its master sets the slide size and `unit-scale`.

background.description: The background every slide shows, unless the slide sets its own.

transition.description: The transition from every slide to the next, unless the slide sets its own. Left out, slides cross-dissolve over 0.5 seconds.

soundtrack.description: Music that plays under the whole presentation.

file.description: The audio file, as a presentation's file path.

loop.description: `repeat` plays it again from the start when it ends. Left out, it plays once.

fade-in.description: How long it takes to rise from silence.

fade-out.description: How long it takes to fall to silence at the end.

self-playing.description: Settings for playing the presentation on its own, as at a kiosk.

slide-delay.description: How long each slide stays after its last step before the next one.

step-delay.description: How long the presentation waits before each step that would wait for a click.

loop.description: `repeat` starts it over after the last slide. Left out, it stops there.

countdown.description: How long the talk should take, in seconds. The presenter's timer counts down from it.

anyOf.description: What a new text box starts with. Without this key, or with an empty record, a new text box takes the body style. `"none"` gives it none.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

default-text-style.description: The text style and color of a new text box, or none for no style.

image-style.description: The style a generated image object is made in when it sets none of its own, as text, or `none` for no style. Left out, it's none. A background's picture takes `background-image-style` instead.

background-image-style.description: The style a generated background image is made in when its background sets none of its own, as text, or `none` for no style. Left out, it's MarkdownPoint's own.

swatches.description: The colors the author has saved for this presentation, as hex colors.

date.description: The date the date field shows, as YYYY-MM-DD. It must be a real calendar date, from year 0001 on.

locale.description: The presentation's language and region, as a BCP 47 language tag, such as fr-CA, which MarkdownPoint writes canonical. Dates are written and its own chart cells read by it. Left out, it is en-US.

additionalProperties.description: One slide's objects, look, and animation. Its text is in the .md file.

layout.description: The theme layout the slide uses, by key.

scheme.description: The slide's color scheme. Left out, it uses its layout's. One the theme lacks stays as written, and the slide shows its layout's, or light, until the theme has it again.

background.description: The slide's own background, shown in place of the presentation's whole: a key it leaves out takes its default, and an empty one is plain.

skipped.description: Whether the slide is skipped when presenting and exporting. It stays in the presentation.

transition.description: The transition from this slide to the next, or none.

anyOf.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object’s frame

size.description: How far past the letters the shadow reaches, as Photoshop's Size.

spread.description: The share of the size by which what casts the shadow grows solid before the rest of the size blurs, as Photoshop's Spread, where 1 stands solid all the way out.

offset.description: How far it falls from the letters, as {x, y} across and down.

color.description: Its color: a color role or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. The color carries no opacity, not even a role's: `opacity` alone sets how opaque the shadow is.

The camera's motion blur. Only the 3D layer blurs, and only in exported movies and the Agent's rendered frames. The editor, presentations, and still exports stay sharp.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open, in frames of the movie. 0 draws no blur. Left out, it's 0.5. A step can animate it.

frame-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the shutter's opening. Left out, it's center.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open, then averaged, as Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples. More give smoother streaks but take longer. Left out, it's 32.

anyOf.description: The camera's render effects, as Cinema 4D's Render Settings add Global Illumination and Ambient Occlusion: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces and of the World's light closed off where they meet. It shows wherever the 3D layer does: in the editor, presentations, exports, and movies. Only surfaces in view bounce light, and a shadow catcher bounces none. An override replaces the whole record. Each key may be left out.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what stands near them. Left out, it's false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other, and a shadow catcher darkens where an object stands on it. Left out, it's false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface. Left out, it's 400.

anyOf.description: The camera's drift: a slow move that comes to rest on the camera's set position. It runs on the slide's own clock. It starts when the slide's transition in begins and runs through the slide's steps, waits, and transition out. A blank screen pauses it. The camera and its target move together from `from` toward the set position. At t seconds they stand `from` × (1 − t ÷ `duration`)² away from it. So they start at full speed, slow steadily, and come to rest when `duration` ends. The editor, PDFs, and still exports show the set position. A slide that a scroll transition enters or leaves shows no drift, with a warning, since two drifting cameras would meet at the seam.

from.description: Where the camera starts, as an {x, y, z} offset from its set position. An axis left out doesn't move.

duration.description: How many seconds after the slide begins to appear the camera comes to rest. A drift plays once, so it must end.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object, as Cinema 4D's Position constraint does. Only the camera takes it. With a spring, the camera follows the way a keyframe's spring moves: it trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. Keys other than id, type, and target may be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as follow, unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as constraints.follow.strength.

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows.

target-node.description: The name of a node in the target's model, such as ball. The camera follows it where the model's Action moves it. Left out, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: The 3D space's axes the camera follows on, of x, y, and z. Left out, all three.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera's position counts from the target's point instead of the slide's center at z 0, as Blender's Copy Location Offset adds it. Left out, it's true. False puts it at the target's point.

strength.description: How far the camera moves to the target's point, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. Left out, it's 1. A step can animate it.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on, written as a keyframe's `spring` interpolation is: its `amount` and `response`. Left out, the camera follows exactly.

amount.description: How far the camera swings past where the target stops, from 0, not at all, to 1.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter response catches up sooner.

overrides.description: Changes, by id, to what the slide inherits from its layout and master, kept even when equal to it. `null` removes one, except the camera and the World.

file.description: a file path in the presentation’s folder

objects.description: The slide's objects, back to front. Its own are written out, and one from its layout or master appears as its id. One it inherits and doesn't name stands behind them all.

initial.description: The values of animated parameters before the slide's first step, as "object.parameter" keys such as "card.opacity".

slides.description: The slides, by id. The .md file has their order and text.

additionalProperties.description: A reusable animated scene that slides show as instances. A composition can't contain itself, directly or through another.

name.description: The composition's name, on one line.

scheme.description: The color scheme it is drawn in on its own canvas, where it is edited. Left out, it uses the light scheme. Each instance takes the scheme of the slide it stands on.

additionalProperties.description: One control a composition offers its instances, by an id unique among its controls. A binding, an instance's value and a marker name the control by its id, which a rename keeps. Its default matches its type: a number, true or false, a color, one of its options, or a file path for a media control. The objects a media control binds are of one media kind, and its default and values are of that kind. A property a choice control sets reads the name its option spells: the words in lowercase, with a hyphen for each run of spaces, so "Top left" spells top-left. No two options spell one name, as Left and left would.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line and not empty. A rename changes only the name, and two controls may share one.
The name the author sees, on one line and not empty. A rename changes only the name, and two controls may share one.

default.description: The value used when an instance sets none. A number control's default lies from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

min.description: A number control's smallest value, below its max.

max.description: A number control's largest value, above its min.

items.description: one line with no spaces at the start or end and no comma

options.description: A choice control's options, one or more, each words on one line with no space at either end and no comma: ",", "，" or "、".

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line and not empty. A rename changes only the name, and two controls may share one.

default.description: The value used when an instance sets none. A number control's default lies from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

controls.description: What each instance can set, by control id.

objects.description: Its objects, back to front. A composition can't hold a model, a light, a shadow catcher, a floor, a camera, the World, or a text with a `model`.

initial.description: The values of animated parameters before its first step, as "object.parameter" keys.

steps.description: Its steps, played back to back. They take no cues and no `loop-from`. Every pass counted, they last at most 4,294,967,296 seconds.

compositions.description: Reusable animated scenes, by id. Slides show them as instances.

additionalProperties.description: A comment thread pinned to a slide or a composition, stored under an id unique among the presentation's threads. A thread stays when its slide or composition is deleted.

slide.description: The id of the slide it is pinned to.

composition.description: The id of the composition it is pinned to.

created.description: When it was written, as a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says, as text that isn't blank, without control characters but line breaks and tabs.

position.description: Where it is pinned, as {x, y} fractions of the slide or composition.

resolved.description: Whether the thread is resolved. Left out, it isn't.

additionalProperties.description: One reply in a comment thread, stored under an id unique in its thread.

created.description: When it was written, as a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says, as text that isn't blank, without control characters but line breaks and tabs.

replies.description: The replies, by id, each with an author, a created time, and text, written in the order they were made, then by id, so a new reply adds lines at the end. Left out, there are none.

comments.description: Comment threads, by id, written in the order they were made, then by id. Each names the slide or composition it is pinned to.

anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about when it is animated or given an initial value, and the point a group tilts about.

x.description: How far across the frame, as a fraction of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame, as a fraction of its height.

auto-layout.description: How a group places its members one after another. Keys left out default to direction vertical, gap 0, align start, and reference point start. Members are placed in their order in the `objects` list. Hidden members, members with `ignore-auto-layout`, and lines attached to an object are skipped.

direction.description: Whether the members run down or across.

gap.description: The space between one member and the next.

align.description: How the members line up across the layout's direction.

reference-point.description: Which point of the members' box along the layout's direction stays at the position as they grow or shrink: its start, its middle, or its end.

position.description: The slide point, as {x, y}, where the members' box stands: its top-left corner in the group's turn, or its middle or end along the layout's direction by the reference point.

background.description: A slide background: a fill, an image, or an image on a fill.

fill.description: The color or gradient behind everything.

image.description: An image over the fill, as a presentation's file path.

crop.description: How far the image is zoomed, and the point it keeps in view.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated background image.

image-style.description: The style of a generated background image, as text, or `none` for no style. Left out, it's the presentation's `background-image-style`.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated background image is made with a transparent background.

restyle.description: A library style applied over the image, which MarkdownPoint draws from the image as first made.

generation.description: Which image generation record made the background image, and for a restyle the image it was applied to.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the image.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is, from −1 to 1. 0 leaves it unchanged.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has, from −1 to 1. 0 leaves it unchanged.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are, from −1 to 1. 0 leaves them unchanged.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are, from −1 to 1. 0 leaves them unchanged.

grayscale.description: How far the image's colors fade to gray. 0 leaves them unchanged.

color.description: a color role or a hex color

id.description: Who wrote it, if known: `local:` and a lowercase UUID for a computer's user, `shared:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits for a collaboration service member, or `dropbox:` and a Dropbox account id.

name.description: The author's name, as the thread shows it, as text that isn't blank, without control characters.

anyOf.description: A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target, as Cinema 4D's Aim constraint does. Keys other than id, type, and target may be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as look, unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as constraints.look.strength.

owner-node.description: The name of the model's node that turns, such as Head. Left out, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light whose origin it turns toward, or `camera` to turn toward the camera.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target, in its GLB's axes: y is up, and a model faces along +z. Left out, it's y.

strength.description: How far it turns toward the target, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. It acts on the result of the constraints before it. Left out, it's 1. A step can animate it.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as it scales, in the model's Local space. Volume is measured at the model's scale before animation. Keys other than id and type may be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as squash, unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as constraints.squash.strength.

mode.description: When the volume is kept. `strict` keeps it under any scale. `uniform` keeps it while the model scales evenly. `single-axis` keeps it while the free axis alone scales. Left out, it's strict.

free-axis.description: The axis whose scale is animated. The other two follow to keep the volume. Left out, it's y.

volume.description: The volume to keep, as a multiple of the model's volume before animation. Left out, it's 1.

strength.description: How strongly it keeps the volume, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. Left out, it's 1. A step can animate it.

crop.description: An image's or a video's zoom and focus inside its frame.

scale.description: How far it is zoomed. At 1 the image sits in its frame as its scale-mode sets. Above 1 it zooms in. Below 1 it zooms out.

focal-point.description: The point it keeps in view, {x, y}, each a fraction of the image across and down. A step animates crop.focal-point.x and .y.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow, as Photoshop's Drop Shadow sets one: what the object paints grows solid by size × spread, then blurs by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. Its size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far it reaches, in canvas units, at most the widest the exported PDF draws as the canvas does: 102.878569 up to a shorter side of 1080, in proportion beyond, as 205.757138 at 3840 × 2160.

spread.description: The share of the size by which what casts the shadow grows solid before the rest of the size blurs, as Photoshop's Spread, where 1 stands solid all the way out.

offset.description: How far it falls from the object, as {x, y} across and down.

color.description: Its color: a color role or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. The color carries no opacity, not even a role's: `opacity` alone sets how opaque the shadow is.

enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece. Keys left out default to interpolation linear, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 1. Delivered by paragraph, a paragraph no cue names stands from the start. A text with a `text-path` stands on one line, with no paragraph to deliver apart: a reader warns of delivery by paragraph there, and the text enters all at once.

delivery.description: `by-paragraph`: each paragraph enters on the step whose text cue names it. It takes based-on `paragraph`, no seed, and order, spread, pause, and progress only at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter, in seconds. With interpolation hold, each paragraph shows as its cue is reached. A step that holds only paragraphs' cues lasts as long as they take.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter: opacity, x and y, scale, rotation, and blur.

x.description: How far across it starts, in ems.

y.description: How far down it starts, in ems.

scale.description: Its scale, where 1 is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned, in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is, its radius in ems. On the slide, it blurs no wider than the slide's widest blur, as `blur` says.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually on a curve, or at once with hold. A spring's response and an elastic's period don't apply here.

fade.description: The fade of each piece, as `{ length }`, a share of its travel. It follows the piece's interpolation.

length.description: How much of the piece's entrance the fade lasts, as a fraction. The fade starts with the move.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece and takes a turn. Only based-on `character` takes it.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in.

seed.description: The seed for a random order. The same seed always gives the same order, by the rule the introduction gives.

spread.description: How many pieces are in motion at once.

pause.description: A pause between paragraphs, as long as this many pieces take to enter.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. Steps animate it.

exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece. Keys left out default to interpolation linear, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 0.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting: opacity, x and y, scale, rotation, and blur.

x.description: How far across it ends, in ems.

y.description: How far down it ends, in ems.

scale.description: Its scale, where 1 is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned, in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is, its radius in ems. On the slide, it blurs no wider than the slide's widest blur, as `blur` says.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually on a curve, or at once with hold. A spring's response and an elastic's period don't apply here.

fade.description: The fade of each piece, as `{ length }`, a share of its travel. It follows the piece's interpolation.

length.description: How much of the piece's exit the fade lasts, as a fraction. The fade ends with the move.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece and takes a turn. Only based-on `character` takes it.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in.

seed.description: The seed for a random order. The same seed always gives the same order, by the rule the introduction gives.

spread.description: How many pieces are in motion at once.

pause.description: A pause between paragraphs, as long as this many pieces take to exit.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. Steps animate it.

flat-scale.description: A flat object's scale along its own axes, about its frame's center. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

floor-position.description: A floor's height in the 3D space. It takes y alone: a floor lies level and stretches without end, as Cinema 4D's Floor does, so it moves only up and down. Left out, the floor lies on the slide's bottom edge.

y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge, in canvas units.

frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only its x and y: the table is as wide as its columns and as tall as its rows. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text: its width when `auto-size` grows the width, unless the text follows a path or has more than one column, and its height when `auto-size` grows the height, unless the text follows a path. Its x and y then place the box with no length along those sides. The text grows from that box's center, and the box turns and scales about it: the point its alignment holds at mid-height when the width grows (the left edge, the middle, or the right edge, and a justified text's start side), the middle of its top edge when the height grows, and the point its alignment holds on its top edge when both grow. So `auto-size`, `align`, `text-direction`, `column-count`, `text-path`, `rotation`, and `scale` decide which point x and y name. An override that changes one of them on a box that grows, or that it makes grow, gives each of x and y that would name another point for any size of its text. Each one it leaves out keeps what the box inherits.

x.description: Where the left edge is, across. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

y.description: Where the top edge is, down. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

generation.description: How a generated or restyled image was made: the image shown is the one its image generation record made.

id.description: The id of the image generation record that made the image shown, the lowercase UUID its file `generated/<id>.json` is named by.

original.description: The image a restyle was applied to, there only when the record is a restyle's.

file.description: Its file path, as a presentation's file path, ending in an image's extension.

generation.description: How it was made, when it was generated. Left out, it wasn't.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction, in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line lies, in the object's frame; the angle turns it about its middle. Left out, the line crosses the box the gradient fills through its center, as CSS's gradient line does.

x.description: Its middle's x, as a fraction of the frame's width.

y.description: Its middle's y, as a fraction of the frame's height.

length.description: Its length, as a fraction of the frame's diagonal.

stops.description: The gradient's colors, two or more, each with its position.

center.description: Where a radial gradient centers, as {x, y}.

line-end.description: A line end attached to an object. Its last position reaches further than a point, since an object at the edge of the canvas can have its side past a point's range.

object.description: The id of the object it attaches to.

side.description: Which side of the object it attaches to, or the nearest.

last-position.description: Where the end was when last drawn, as {x, y}. It's used when the object it attaches to isn't on the slide.

One unit of the model is one em of the text's size, and its origin stands on the first line's baseline at the left of the text's column. It moves, turns and scales with the text's frame, its depth by the square root of the text's two scales.

bevel.description: How far the letters' edges are rounded, in ems. 0 leaves them sharp.

poster.description: a file path in the presentation’s folder

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without opacity, such as "#000000"

repeater.description: Copies of the object, each moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. A turned object's copies run along its own axes: their position, anchor point and position randomness turn with its rotation. Keys left out default to 0, except `scale` and `end-opacity`, which are 1, and `anchor-point`, the frame's center. A shape with text can't repeat. A group repeats only when each member can, or is a line with no end attached to an object outside the group.

copies.description: How many there are, the original included.

position.description: How far each copy moves from the one before, as {x, y} across and down. A step animates them as repeater.position.x and repeater.position.y.

rotation.description: How far each copy turns from the one before, clockwise.

scale.description: How much each copy scales from the one before, where 1 keeps its size.

anchor-point.description: The point the copies turn and scale about, {x, y}, each a fraction of the frame across and down.

stagger.description: How much later each copy plays the object's animation than the one before.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity, as a fraction of the object's own. The copies between fade toward it.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random, as a fraction of its size.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random.

seed.description: The random seed. The same seed always gives the same variation, by the rule the introduction gives.

restyle.description: A library style, applied over an image or a background's image.

name.description: The style's name, on one line.

reference-prompt.description: The prompt for the style's example image, as text that isn't blank.

prompt.description: How the style changes an image, as an edit prompt that isn't blank.

transparent-background.description: Whether images in the style have transparent backgrounds.

space-euler.description: A 3D object's turn about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. In degrees it turns in Cinema 4D's HPB order: heading about y, then pitch about its own x, then bank about its own z, as three.js's YXZ Euler composes them. Each turns counterclockwise looking along its axis toward the origin: a positive z turns it counterclockwise on the slide, a positive x tilts its top toward the viewer, and a positive y brings its left side forward. A group's rotation-x and a flat object's rotation, clockwise, turn the other way, in the slide's axes, where y points down, and its rotation-y the same way. At zero rotation, a model faces the viewer, as its glTF file faces +z, and a light shines and the camera looks along its own −z, into the slide. Its own y then points up. In quaternion mode it holds w, x, y, and z, the same turn as glTF's quaternion with w first, each part divided by the quaternion's length as written, then read to six decimal places. A quaternion whose length as written is 0 is refused. Its keyframes then turn it whole: each keyframe of `<object>.rotation` is such an orientation, read the same way, and the turn between two keyframes goes the shorter way round at its interpolation's pace. In degrees, rotation.x, rotation.y, and rotation.z animate each turn on its own, so a keyframe can spin it more than once. Blender's axes differ, with z up. For a model exported from Blender to glTF with +Y up, write Blender's quaternion (w, x, y, z) as (w, x, z, −y). To copy degrees, first set Blender's rotation mode to YXZ. Then x here is Blender's X, y is Blender's Z, and z is Blender's −Y. At zero rotation, Blender's camera and lights point down, along their own −Z. Convert theirs as a model's, then turn it −90° about its own x, as Blender's glTF exporter does. As a quaternion, that's (w, x, z, −y) times (0.707107, −0.707107, 0, 0), with the second on the right. In degrees, when Blender's Y is 0, as it is for a level horizon, x is Blender's X minus 90, y is Blender's Z, and z is 0.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-position.description: A point in the 3D space, in canvas units. x runs right from the slide's left edge, y up from its bottom edge, and z toward the viewer, and the slide lies at z 0. The space is right-handed, as glTF and three.js define it. A parented model's, light's, shadow catcher's or camera's position and target are in its parent's space, through its parent-inverse where it has one, and a parented shadow catcher's width and height too. A parented object's world is its parent's world, or that of the parent's node its parent-node names, times its parent-inverse, times its own position, rotation, and scale, each matrix acting on a column of x, y, z, and 1 to its right: `world = parent × parent-inverse × local`, as Blender's Parent Inverse composes them. Its own constraints apply after. A parented camera turns with its parent, never scales with it, and a target camera banks with it. The camera's position may leave out any part. Left out, its x and y center it on the slide, and its z puts it where the slide shows at full size. A target gives all three parts, the camera's too.

w.description: A quaternion's w, in quaternion mode only.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-scale.description: A 3D object's scale along its own axes, about its origin. A negative scale mirrors it along that axis. A light's scale also scales the objects parented to it, and an area light's surface.

items.description: One step: the moves, cuts, and media starts that a click or the previous step sets off. Every time in a step, and in its keyframes and cues, is in seconds, rounded to six decimal places. Sums of times and the times shown are rounded the same way. A step has no delay of its own: a keyframe's start delays its move. A first step that starts by itself plays after the slide's transition. A scroll plays the next slide's first step with it, whatever its start. A step that repeats plays alone on its click, and a file that breaks that reads with a warning, without the repeat. A step after one that loops while waiting starts when that step's first pass ends, and the loop plays on under it.

id.description: The step's id, unique on its slide.

name.description: The step's name in the Animate list, on one line.

start.description: When the step starts: with the previous step, or after it ends. On the first step, either starts it when the slide's transition ends, except under a scroll. Left out, it waits for a click.

min-duration.description: The least time the step lasts, in seconds. A later keyframe, cue, or entering paragraph extends it, and left out or 0, the step lasts as long as what it holds.

repeat.description: How many times the step plays before it completes. Left out, it plays once.

loop-from.description: Seconds into the step that it loops back to while waiting for the next click: before the later of its `min-duration` and its keyframe and cue times, not counting a paragraph's entrance.

additionalProperties.description: One property's animation in a step: its keyframes and what happens after the last one. A position can also be keyed as one point: `frame.xy` and `translation.xy` hold {x, y}, and `position.xyz` holds {x, y, z}, each keyframe holding every part, as a move along a motion path is keyed. A step keys a position as a point or by its parts, not both: a step that keys both reads with a warning, and the point plays. An initial value sets each part on its own.

items.description: One keyframe: a value a property reaches at a time. Two keyframes of one property at one time read with a warning, and the later id plays. A color moves in sRGB, a role as the slide's scheme colors it. Its opacity moves straight, and its red, green, and blue each weigh by the opacity at either end, as premultiplied alpha blends them, so a color fading out to a transparent one keeps its own color as it fades. Each frame's color is rounded to 8 bits per channel.

id.description: The keyframe's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

start.description: When the move into the keyframe begins, in seconds into the step. It must come before time. Left out, it begins at the previous keyframe.

time.description: When the property reaches the value, in seconds into the step.

value.description: The value, written as the property is. `null` clears a property an object may leave out, so its text style or default shows.

interpolation.description: How the value reaches the keyframe: gradually on a curve, or at once with hold. It's a named curve, a named curve with its settings, a cubic Bézier, or a spring. Left out, linear.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts. Up to this keyframe, the motion follows that move's curve.

end.description: When it would have ended, in seconds into the step, at or after the keyframe's time.

path.description: A curved motion path for the move into the keyframe. It goes on a point keyframe.

geometry.description: The path, as SVG path data from the move's start, 0 0, to its end, 1 0. It is one open contour of 2 to 8,192 points, in at most 1,048,576 characters.

orient.description: Whether the object turns to face along the path.

exponential-scale.description: Whether a scale move changes by a steady ratio over time, so a zoom looks even; from or to 0, or across it, it moves at an even pace. Only a scale parameter takes it.

oscillate.description: A wave added to the value from this keyframe to the next, or to the step's end. On a looping curve, the wave plays again each time around.

amplitude.description: How far the value swings either way, in the property's own unit.

frequency.description: How many full cycles each second. A noise wave's cycle is one stretch of its noise, as the introduction gives it.

phase.description: Where in its cycle the wave starts, 360 degrees to a cycle, as the introduction gives each wave and its noise. Left out, it's 0.

wave-shape.description: The wave's shape, each as the introduction gives it. Left out, it's sine.

seed.description: The noise seed. The same seed always gives the same noise, by the rule the introduction gives. Left out, it's 0.

loop.description: How it loops after its last keyframe until the step ends: `repeat` replays from `loop-keyframe` to the last, and `ping-pong` plays that back and forth. Left out, it plays once.

loop-keyframe.description: The id of the keyframe the loop starts at, where its move begins if it has a `start`. Left out, or naming no keyframe of the curve, it is the first. It needs `loop`.

curves.description: The step's animation, by object and parameter, such as card.opacity.

items.description: An event at a set time in a step. A clip names the model's Action as every reader names the file's animations, in file order: a name the file gives, not empty, is kept and matched exactly, and every such name is reserved first, wherever it stands in the file; an animation with no name, or an empty one, is Animation and its number in the file, from 1, as Animation 1; an animation whose name an earlier one has, or whose generated name is reserved or already given, takes the first of name 2, name 3 and on not yet taken, a space before the number. So Walk, Walk, Walk 2 read as Walk, Walk 3, Walk 2, and an unnamed first animation beside a given Animation 1 reads as Animation 1 2.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on.

paragraph.description: The id of the paragraph that appears, as `<!-- id: … -->` ends its last line; a reader warns of an id no paragraph of the text carries.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on.

action.description: The name of the model's Action that a clip plays. An unnamed Action is Animation and its number in the file, Animation 1; a name the file repeats or gives another Action takes 2, 3 in file order.

loop.description: `repeat` plays the Action again from its start each time it ends. Left out, it plays once.

clip-trim.description: The part of the Action that plays, as a start and an end in seconds into the Action.

stride.description: How far the model travels per cycle of its Action, in the GLB's meters. The Action's timing then follows the model's travel, so planted feet don't slide.

blend-in.description: How long the clip takes to blend in fully over the model's current motion. Left out, it is fully blended in from its start.

clip-scale.description: How much longer a clip's Action plays than its file says, as Maya's Clip Scale: 2 is half speed, 0.5 double. Left out, it's 1. A clip with a stride ignores it.

cues.description: Events at set times in the step: a paragraph appearing, an audio object, a video, or a web video starting, or a clip playing a model's Action.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color sits along the gradient, 0 to 1. Left out, the ends sit at 0 and 1, and the stops between spread evenly. A stop never stands before the one ahead of it.

table-frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only its x and y: the table is as wide as its columns and as tall as its rows. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text: its width when `auto-size` grows the width, unless the text follows a path or has more than one column, and its height when `auto-size` grows the height, unless the text follows a path. Its x and y then place the box with no length along those sides. The text grows from that box's center, and the box turns and scales about it: the point its alignment holds at mid-height when the width grows (the left edge, the middle, or the right edge, and a justified text's start side), the middle of its top edge when the height grows, and the point its alignment holds on its top edge when both grow. So `auto-size`, `align`, `text-direction`, `column-count`, `text-path`, `rotation`, and `scale` decide which point x and y name. An override that changes one of them on a box that grows, or that it makes grow, gives each of x and y that would name another point for any size of its text. Each one it leaves out keeps what the box inherits.

x.description: Where the left edge is, across. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

y.description: Where the top edge is, down. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

x.description: How far across the frame, as a fraction of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame, as a fraction of its height.

text-frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only its x and y: the table is as wide as its columns and as tall as its rows. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text: its width when `auto-size` grows the width, unless the text follows a path or has more than one column, and its height when `auto-size` grows the height, unless the text follows a path. Its x and y then place the box with no length along those sides. The text grows from that box's center, and the box turns and scales about it: the point its alignment holds at mid-height when the width grows (the left edge, the middle, or the right edge, and a justified text's start side), the middle of its top edge when the height grows, and the point its alignment holds on its top edge when both grow. So `auto-size`, `align`, `text-direction`, `column-count`, `text-path`, `rotation`, and `scale` decide which point x and y name. An override that changes one of them on a box that grows, or that it makes grow, gives each of x and y that would name another point for any size of its text. Each one it leaves out keeps what the box inherits.

x.description: Where the left edge is, across. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

y.description: Where the top edge is, down. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

time-trim.description: The part of a video or audio file, or of a model's Action, that plays.

start.description: Where it starts, in seconds into the file or the Action. Left out, it's 0.

end.description: Where it ends, in seconds into the file or the Action. It must come after start. Left out, it plays to the end.

transition.description: A slide transition. A scroll moves both slides along one strip. Each slide's 3D objects keep their index in its stacking order and are clipped at its edge. A model or 3D text with the same id on both slides crosses between them whole. Neither slide's camera drifts during a scroll. During any other transition, both cameras drift. Keys left out default to interpolation ease-in-out, match object, direction left, color black, and delay 0.

start.description: When it starts. Left out, it starts on a click. `automatically` starts it after the slide's last step.

delay.description: For a transition that starts by itself, how long it waits after the slide's last step ends.

duration.description: How long it takes. With effect `none`, it's left out.

delay.description: For a transition that starts by itself, how long it waits after the slide's last step ends.

interpolation.description: How the transition speeds up and slows down. Only `carry-over` and `scroll` take it.

match.description: What `carry-over` matches between two texts: whole objects, words, or characters.

utc-time.description: a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as "2026-10-17T19:30:00.000Z"

wipe.description: A reveal behind a moving straight edge.

progress.description: How much of the object shows: 0 none, 1 all.

angle.description: Which way the edge travels, in degrees clockwise from up. The angle turns with the object.
